YuE2 Studio - quick guide

First start

  1. Setup & Server tab → Download engine (~300 MB).
  2. Tick the models (default: Q8_0 main model, VAE F16, SheetSage2) → Download selected (~6 GB). The download can be stopped and resumed later.
  3. ▶ Start - the server starts (green = running). Later it starts automatically.
  4. Generate tab → lyrics + style → Queue and generate.

Lyrics

Sections in square brackets, on their own line: [Intro] [Verse] [Pre-Chorus] [Chorus] [Bridge] [Outro]. Short lines, the chorus repeated word for word. YuE2 learned mostly in English - other languages can work, but pronunciation is weaker. For a track without vocals: [instrumental] + the Instrumental checkbox.

Style

Comma-separated English tags, ideally 5–8. Recommended order: language, genre, mood, instruments, vocal type, production. E.g. English, delta blues, smoky, slide guitar, harmonica, raspy male vocal, live recording

COT mode

offNo music plan - fastest, for sketches.
melodyMakes a melody plan (ABC), or follows your ABC.
fullMelody + chord plan - the best structure. Default.

ABC score

The generated plan is saved for every melody/full track (.abc). On the ABC tab you can edit it, extend it ×2/×3 (the parts stay in sync), delete the vocal part (against humming in instrumentals), or extract it from an existing song with SheetSage2. Then tick “Use ABC score” on the Generate tab.

Important parameters

Guidance scaleHow strictly it follows the description. Too high → artifacts.
Inference stepsSound synthesis steps (default 8). More → slower, sometimes cleaner.
Semantic max tokensRaises/lowers the maximum length of the track (default 9000). The Song length slider is easier.
TemperatureHigher = more creative, less predictable.
Repetition penaltyIf the music gets “stuck”, raise it a little.

For parameters without a tick, the model's own default applies.

Models and VRAM (16 GB)

  • Q8_0: recommended, runs comfortably with ~12 GB VRAM.
  • Q4_0: less memory, slightly lower quality.
  • BF16: best quality, the most accurate base for LoRAs - needs more VRAM.
  • The server automatically unloads between YuE2 and SheetSage2 (Settings).

LoRA

AR LoRA: changes the planning/semantics (e.g. the instrumental adapter, needs full COT). NAR LoRA: the sound (e.g. “realaudio” v4). Only non-ComfyUI (unfused) .safetensors files work. Switching LoRAs reloads the model (automatically).

Queue

Several generations can be queued (also with the Count field). The running job can only be stopped with Abort now (server restart).

Projects and clean slate

At the top is the project bar: a project = the contents of every tab + the songs generated for it. 🆕 New project (Ctrl+N) – every tab is cleared, new name. 💾 Save (Ctrl+S) – into one .y2proj file. 📂 Open (Ctrl+O) / Recent – comes back exactly. The ● mark: unsaved changes. Nothing is lost when you quit: next time you continue where you left off.

🧹 Clean slate on every working tab: clears only that tab. The Library shows only the current project's songs by default; 🧹 Clear library… deletes songs (from the list only, or from disk too).

Remake – an existing song in a new style

  1. Browse… – MP3/WAV/FLAC… For a long song tick Only a section (60–90 s is ideal).
  2. ⚡ Steps 2–4 in one go – vocal separation (HTDemucs), melody + chords (SheetSage2), lyrics recognition (Qwen3-ASR).
  3. Timed recognition (on by default) splits the lyrics into lines at the singer's breaths – so they fit the melody better. The ⏱ Timing… button shows at which second / bar each line is heard in the original. Don't write times into the lyrics: YuE2 doesn't understand them and would sing them.
  4. Check the recognized lyrics – correct them, write new ones, or have them translated (Ollama).
  5. Tick one or more styles, choose a voice and the vocal language.
  6. ▶ Start remake – N variants per style. Double click on the right to listen.

Needed: the SheetSage2, HTDemucs and Qwen3-ASR packages (Setup tab). If one is missing, that step is skipped (you can type the lyrics by hand). YuE2 follows the melody and the mood – it's not an exact copy, but a new cover.

DAW – track editor

  • Loading: ＋ Audio file…, ＋ From Library, or the 🎛 To DAW button in the Library.
  • Split into tracks: ✂ button (or right click a clip) – 4 tracks: vocals, drums, bass, other. Needs the HTDemucs package (Setup tab). The original track is muted.
  • Clips: drag to move (to another track too), drag the edges to trim, use the white dots on top to fade in/out. S = cut at the playhead, Del = delete, Ctrl+D = duplicate, double click = properties (tempo %, pitch, reverse, volume).
  • Track header: M = mute, S = solo, A = volume automation (curve on the track: click = point, right click = delete), FX = effect chain (EQ, compressor, reverb, delay, chorus, distortion…, ready chains for vocals/drums/bass).
  • Master: volume and Master FX (e.g. limiter) on the whole mix.
  • Ruler: click = jump, drag = loop range (switch on with 🔁).
  • MIDI: right click a clip → MIDI score (needs the MuScriptor package).
  • Export: the mix to a WAV/MP3/FLAC file (can be added to the Library), or each track separately.
  • Undo: Ctrl+Z, redo: Ctrl+Y. The DAW content is part of the project.

Score

  • Source: the ABC score tab, the plan of the song selected in the Library (🎼 Score button), or a MIDI file (e.g. one made in the DAW: right click a clip → ♫ MIDI score).
  • For MIDI: Melody (one staff, for vocals) or Piano (two staves) type, rhythm grid, key.
  • Transpose, size, title, composer, part selection, chord symbols on/off.
  • 🖨 Print, save as PDF, MIDI and ABC, ▶ Play with the notes highlighted (the instrument sounds need internet), open in MuseScore.
  • The score viewer (abcjs) is downloaded on first use.

Guide

With the 🧭 Guide button at the bottom or the buttons at the top you can start step-by-step tours: on the dark layer focus on the highlighted element (you can click it too). Step: Next / → ; exit: Esc.

Interface language

Settings tab → Interface language. The translations are in the lang folder (JSON files) and can be corrected with any text editor.
